title: Independent audit of OpenAI's October 2026 AI-generated mathematics
description:
An independent audit of selected unformalized results from OpenAI's October 2026 collection of AI-generated mathematics manuscripts (github.com/openai/math), plus Lean 4 formalizations of some combinatorial parts (Hindman's sum-product problem, result 164: Lemma 2.5 and Corollary 1.2, with a self-contained finite Ramsey theorem).

The audits and the Lean code were written by Anthropic's Claude (Opus 5.5; most November 2026 work by Fable 5.1 and 5.2) acting as research agents, under the direction of the repository owner, who is not a professional mathematician. Findings were re-checked against the LaTeX sources and reviewed independently by OpenAI's Codex (GPT-6.1); that review overturned one original finding, which is kept in the repository as a withdrawn finding. No finding has been reviewed by a domain expert. Please treat them as leads for experts, not as verdicts. Audit reports are in Japanese.

v1.1.0 adds four audits of unformalized results (138 Subset Sum in 2^{0.49n}, 109 integer multiplication below n log n, 321 counterexample to Wall's D(2) problem, 285 counterexample to the Kadison–Kaplansky projection conjecture) and a second independent Codex review of the two strongest inferences (109, 321), which downgraded the first and corrected a theorem-numbering error in our report on the second.

v1.2.0 adds four audits of unformalized results (142 deterministic polynomial factorization over F_p, 178 deterministic nonbipartite Ramanujan graphs, 266 N(6) = 3 for mutually unbiased bases with its companion paper on exact Fourier certificates, 268 the periodic spin-one Haldane gap), second passes on the core of 029 (the zero-free strip implying a quasi-Riemann hypothesis) and on the C++ sources of 266, follow-ups on 029 (numerics over Q(omega), the application sections, and an exact check of its local Lemma 6.2 at one prime of Q(zeta_12)), and a comparison of the reflection proposition of 003 with its printed closed form and constant over Q(omega). No new definite error in the papers was found. Seven further Codex reviews are included; as before, they mostly corrected our wording (overstated claims, one character misclassified as unramified at 3, error estimates called bounds).
